:::{#exm-bic}
#### BIC of nested `mtcars` models

This example computes @def-bic for the four models of @exm-adjusted-r-squared,
with $\nparams$ counted as in @exm-aic.

```{r}
#| label: bic-mtcars
mtcars_bic <- vapply(
  mtcars_fits,
  \(f) {
    -2 * as.numeric(logLik(f)) +
      (length(coef(f)) + 1) * log(nrow(mtcars))
  },
  numeric(1)
)
tibble::tibble(
  predictors = 1:4,
  bic = mtcars_bic,
  r_bic = vapply(mtcars_fits, BIC, numeric(1))
)
```

The `bic` column matches the `r_bic` column that `BIC()` returns: `r isTRUE(all.equal(mtcars_bic, vapply(mtcars_fits, BIC, numeric(1))))`.
The model with `r which.min(mtcars_bic)` predictors has the smallest BIC.
With $\nobs =$ `r nrow(mtcars)`, each parameter costs $\logf{\nobs} =$ `r round(log(nrow(mtcars)), 2)` in BIC against 2 in AIC,
so BIC penalizes each added parameter more heavily than AIC does.

:::
